newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government officials led by Philippine President Fidel Ramos assured the public the arrest of communist leader Felimon Lagman was not the start of a crackdown on critics of the APEC summit (PHILIPPINE STAR,MANILA STANDARD,MALAYA)

- Militant organizations led by the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) threatened to launch large-scale strikes and demonstrations if arrested leftist leader Filemon "Popoy" Lagman is not released (CHRONICLE)

- President Ramos and members of Congress agreed to scrap the ad valorem system and adopt a specific tax scheme saying the move will reduce graft and corruption and raise 31 billion pesos in total revenues over the next four years, House of Representatives Speaker Jose de Venecia said (BULLETIN)
- Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori arrives this afternoon for a four-day visit (BULLETIN)

- President Ramos has declared November 22 to 26 as special holidays in the National Capital Region and Olongapo City due to the APEC summit "to ensure unhampered flow of traffic and to maximize the productive hours of the APEC delegates" (TIMES JOURNAL,BULLETIN,MALAYA)

- The Energy Regulatory Board said at a public hearing by the House Committee on Energy that increases in pump prices of premium and regular gasoline will be suspended until after the justice department has rendered an opinion on the validity of the ERB's formula for increasing prices of oil products in September. Increases in the prices of aviation turbo, liquefied petroleum gasoline, fuel oil and diesel will push through tomorrow (TODAY)

- President Ramos yesterday warned foreigners against joining protest actions during the week-long APEC meeting in Manila and Subic, saying the government is ready to use the full force of the law against them (INQUIRER,TIMES JOURNAL)
